content.text:
I added a delayed reminder job using Inngest. Creating a user now schedules it to log a reminder 10 minutes later, and the job retries if it fails. It hasn't been run end to end. `tsc` and `eslint` showed no errors from the new code. `tsc` does report `Cannot find name 'LayoutProps'` in `src/app/layout.tsx`, which I didn't touch.

I picked Inngest because it handles delays and retries without extra infrastructure, so there's no Redis or worker process to run. It fits a Next.js app, and local dev only needs its dev server.

- **`createUser` is new.** `src/lib/users.ts` had no way to create users, so I added `createUser({ email, name })`. It pushes to the in-memory array and then sends a `notely/user.created` event. If the send fails, it logs the error and the user is still created. Nothing calls `createUser` yet, so you'll need to wire it into your signup flow.
- **The job** is in `src/inngest/functions.ts`. It sleeps 10 minutes, then logs `[reminder] Hi <name> (<email>), user <id> signed up 10 minutes ago.` It retries up to 5 times. The log step is retried on its own, so a failed log doesn't restart the 10-minute wait.
- **Supporting files:** `src/inngest/client.ts` is the shared client. `src/app/api/inngest/route.ts` serves the functions to Inngest.
- **`.env.example`** has placeholder `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` and `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY`, plus a commented `INNGEST_DEV=1` for local use.
- **`.gitignore`:** the existing `.env*` rule would have ignored `.env.example`, so I added `!.env.example`.

To try it locally, set `INNGEST_DEV=1` and run `npx inngest-cli@latest dev` next to `npm run dev`. For production, put real keys from app.inngest.com in your environment.

The user store is in-memory, so users reset on restart. The job only needs the data carried in the event, so it doesn't depend on that store.
